```{r transformationintophyloseqobj}
# Load and create taxon list
load_taxid_list <- function() {
  taxid_list <- read.delim("taxid_list.txt", header = FALSE, sep = "\t", col.names = c("taxid", "species")) #This path has to be changed
  colnames(taxid_list) <- c("taxid", "species")
  taxid_dict <- setNames(taxid_list$taxid, taxid_list$species)
  return(taxid_dict)
}

# Load and process taxonomic info
load_taxonomic_info <- function() {
  taxinf <- read.csv(file.path("Samples_info_dash.txt"), sep = ";", header = FALSE) #This path has to be changed
  colnames(taxinf) <- c("Division", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species")
  return(taxinf)
}

# Load and process genome metadata
load_genome_metadata <- function() {
  metadata <- read.csv("genomes-all_metadata.tsv", sep = "\t")
  metadata_edited <- metadata[, c("Length", "Lineage")]
  metadata_edited <- metadata_edited %>%
    separate(
      Lineage,
      into = c("Division", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species"),
      sep = ";",
      remove = TRUE
    )
  metadata_edited <- metadata_edited[, c("Length", "Species")]
  metadata_edited$Species <- gsub(" ", "_", metadata_edited$Species)
  average_length <- aggregate(Length ~ Species, data = metadata_edited, FUN = mean)
  return(average_length)
}

# Process kraken results
process_kraken_files <- function(list_files_kraken) {
  free_the_krako <- lapply(list_files_kraken, function(x) {
    krakn <- read.csv(x, sep = "\t")
    file_name <- basename(x)
    id <- sub("^(F_\\d+)_.*$", "\\1", file_name)
    
    krakn$multip <- krakn[[ncol(krakn) - 1]] * krakn[[ncol(krakn)]]
    percsam <- paste0("PercSM_", id)
    totreads <- paste0("TotReadsSM_", id)
    colnames(krakn) <- c("Species", "TaxID", "Tax_level", "Krakenrreads", "addedreads", totreads, percsam, "absabd")
    
    krakn <- krakn %>%
      mutate(
        across(everything(), ~ str_trim(.)),
        Species = str_replace_all(Species, " ", "_"),
        Species = paste0("s__", Species)
      ) %>%
      filter(Tax_level == "S")
    
    krakn <- krakn[, c("Species", totreads, percsam)]
    return(krakn)
  })
  
  merged_all <- Reduce(function(x, y) merge(x, y, by = "Species", all = TRUE), free_the_krako)
  return(merged_all)
}

# Normalization by genome length if needed
# Function to merge and normalize Kraken data
merge_and_normalize_data <- function(merged_all, taxinf, average_length, should_merge = TRUE) {
  # Merge taxinf with merged_all by "Species"
  krkan_merged <- merge(taxinf, merged_all, by = "Species")
  
  # Reorder columns to move specific taxonomic columns to the front
  columns_to_move <- c("Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus")
  krkan_merged <- krkan_merged[, c(columns_to_move, setdiff(names(krkan_merged), columns_to_move))]
  
  # Condition to merge with average_length and normalize
  if (should_merge) {
    # Merge with average_length by "Species"
    krkan_merged <- merge(krkan_merged, average_length, by = "Species")
    krkan_merged$Length <- krkan_merged$Length / 1e6  # Convert Length to millions
    
    # Identify columns starting with "TotReads" for normalization
    normalizacio <- grep("^TotReads", colnames(krkan_merged), value = TRUE)
    krkan_merged <- krkan_merged %>%
      mutate(across(all_of(normalizacio), as.numeric))  # Ensure TotReads columns are numeric
    
    # Create new normalized columns by dividing TotReads by Length
    new_columns <- lapply(normalizacio, function(col) {
      krkan_merged[[col]] / krkan_merged$Length
    })
    names(new_columns) <- paste0("Normal_", normalizacio)  # Add "Normal_" prefix to new columns
    krkan_merged <- cbind(krkan_merged, new_columns)  # Append normalized columns to the data frame
  }
  
  # Replace NA values with 0
  krkan_merged[is.na(krkan_merged)] <- 0
  Unfiltered_reads <- grep("^TotReads", colnames(krkan_merged), value = TRUE)
  infoaddedunf <- append(Unfiltered_reads, c("Species", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus"))
  full_krakn_species <- krkan_merged[, infoaddedunf]
  return(full_krakn_species)
}


# Main function for Bracken2Phyloseq
main <- function(project,resultsfolder) {
  taxid_dict <- load_taxid_list()
  taxinf <- load_taxonomic_info()
  average_length <- load_genome_metadata()
  
  list_files_kraken <- list.files(
    path = "{{ input_files.bracken }}",
    pattern = "*.tsv",
    recursive = TRUE,
    full.names = TRUE
  )
  
  merged_all <- process_kraken_files(list_files_kraken)
  krkan_merged <- merge_and_normalize_data(merged_all, taxinf, average_length, should_merge = FALSE)
  
  return(krkan_merged)
}

# Execute main function
results <- main()
taxtablesextract<- read.csv("taxinfo.csv")  #This path has to be changed
sample_info <- read.xlsx("{{ metadata_source.excel_file }}")
process_phyloseq_data <- function(final_results, taxtablesextracted, samples_information) {
  
  # Create OTU matrix
  tax_columns <- c("Species", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus")
  names(final_results) <- gsub("TotReadsSM_", "", names(final_results))
  numeric_columns <- setdiff(colnames(final_results), tax_columns)
  
  otu_mat <- final_results %>%
    tibble::column_to_rownames("Species") %>%
    mutate(across(everything(), as.numeric))   # Convert all columns to numeric
  otu_mat <- otu_mat[, 1:(ncol(otu_mat) - 5)]

  # Create taxa matrix
  tax_mat <- taxtablesextracted %>%
    tibble::column_to_rownames("Species")
  
  # Process metadata
  samples_df <- samples_information %>%
    tibble::column_to_rownames("{{ metadata_source.sample_id_column }}")
  
  # Convert matrix
  otu_mat <- as.matrix(otu_mat)
  tax_mat <- as.matrix(tax_mat)
  
  # Create phyloseq objects
  OTU = otu_table(otu_mat, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)
  TAX = tax_table(tax_mat)
  samples = sample_data(samples_df)
  
  # Final Object
  phyloseq_object = phyloseq(OTU, TAX, samples)
  
  return(phyloseq_object)
}

phyloelement <- process_phyloseq_data(results,taxtablesextract, sample_info)

saveRDS(phyloelement, file = "phyloelement.rds")
```

```{r loadobjects}
# Load phyloseq object
#phyloelement_nofiltered <- readRDS("{{ input_files.phyloseq_object }}")
phyloelement_nofiltered <- phyloelement

# Decontamination step removed per user request (decontam not applied)

# -------------------------
# Prevalence filtering
# -------------------------
filter_prevalence_phyloseq <- function(physeq,
                                       rel_abundance = {{ filtering.rel_abundance }},
                                       prevalence_cutoff = {{ filtering.prevalence_cutoff }},
                                       use_relative = TRUE) {
  otu <- as(otu_table(physeq), "matrix")
  if (!taxa_are_rows(physeq)) {
    otu <- t(otu)
  }
  if (use_relative) {
    otu <- sweep(otu, 2, colSums(otu), "/")
  }
  otu_bin <- otu >= rel_abundance
  prev <- rowSums(otu_bin)
  min_samples <- ceiling(prevalence_cutoff * ncol(otu))
  keep_taxa <- names(prev[prev >= min_samples])
  physeq_filtered <- prune_taxa(keep_taxa, physeq)
  return(physeq_filtered)
}

# Apply prevalence filtering to create working phyloseq object
physeq_filtered <- filter_prevalence_phyloseq(
  phyloelement_nofiltered,
  rel_abundance = {{ filtering.rel_abundance }},
  prevalence_cutoff = {{ filtering.prevalence_cutoff }}
)
```

# Alpha Diversity

Alpha diversity measures the **richness and evenness** of microbial communities within individual samples.

## Shannon Index {.tabset}

Shannon diversity index evaluates **evenness and richness** where higher values indicate greater microbial diversity.

{% for feature in feature_columns %}

### {{ feature }}

```{r shannon{{ loop.index0 }}}

counts <- combined_data %>%
  group_by({{ feature }}) %>%
  summarise(N = n())

p_shannon <- ggboxplot(as.data.frame(combined_data), x = "{{ feature }}", y = "Shannon", fill = "{{ feature }}") +  # Aplica colores personalizados
  geom_jitter(aes(fill = {{ feature }}), 
  position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.025, dodge.width = 0.8),

  ) 


print(p_shannon)
```

# Beta Diversity

Beta diversity measures **compositional differences** between samples, reflecting how microbial communities vary across samples.

```{r betadataprep}

# EXTRACT AND PREPARE CLR-TRANSFORMED OTU DATA

otu_clr <- as(otu_table(clr_phyloelement), 'matrix')

# Ensure OTUs are rows and samples are columns (phyloseq standard format)

if (!taxa_are_rows(clr_phyloelement)) otu_clr <- t(otu_clr)

# CALCULATE AITCHISON DISTANCE (Euclidean distance on CLR-transformed data)

dist_aitchison <- dist(t(otu_clr), method = 'euclidean')

# First analysis: PERFORM PRINCIPAL COORDINATE ANALYSIS (PCoA) ON AITCHISON DISTANCE

pcoa <- cmdscale(dist_aitchison, k=2)

# Convert patient IDs to factor (categorical variable)

patients <- as.factor(sample_data(physeq_filtered)$Patient_ID)

# Second analysis: PERFORM PRINCIPAL COMPONENT ANALYSIS (PCA) ON CLR DATA

# - center = FALSE because CLR data is already centered around zero
# - scale. = TRUE standardizes variables to unit variance
pca <- prcomp(t(otu_clr),
              center = FALSE,
              scale. = TRUE)

# Create data frame with PCA results
pca_df <- data.frame(
  Sample = rownames(pca$x),  # Sample names from PCA scores
  PC1 = pca$x[,1],           # First principal component scores
  PC2 = pca$x[,2]            # Second principal component scores
)

# Set row names for merging
rownames(pca_df) <- pca_df$Sample
pca_df <- merge(pca_df, sam_data, by = "row.names")

# Calculate variance explained by each PC
var_exp <- (pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2)) * 100

# Third analysis: PERFORM UMAP (Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection)
# - Set seed for reproducibility
set.seed(123)

umap_res <- umap(
  t(clr_phyloelement@otu_table),  # Transpose: samples as rows, OTUs as columns
  n_neighbors = 15,               # Size of local neighborhood (higher = more global structure)
  min_dist = 0.1,                 # Minimum distance between points in embedding
  metric = "euclidean"            # Distance metric for UMAP
)

# Create data frame with UMAP results and metadata
umap_df <- data.frame(
  UMAP1 = umap_res[,1],  # First UMAP dimension
  UMAP2 = umap_res[,2],  # Second UMAP dimension
  sample_data(clr_phyloelement)  # All metadata from CLR phyloseq object
)

# Fourth analysis: CALCULATE BRAY-CURTIS DISSIMILARITY
# - Bray-Curtis is a common ecological distance metric

bray_dist <- vegdist(t(otu_table(physeq_filtered)), method = "bray")

# Perform PCoA on Bray-Curtis distance
pcoa_bray_dist <- cmdscale(bray_dist, k=2)
```

{% if analyses.permanova %}

# PERMANOVA Analysis

PERMANOVA (Permutational Multivariate Analysis of Variance) tests whether **inter-group differences** are statistically significant based on multivariate distances.

{% for feature in feature_columns %}

```{r permanova{{ loop.index0 }}}
# PERMANOVA por pares con 9999 permutaciones
pairwise_{{ feature }} <- pairwise.perm.manova(
  dist_aitchison,
  fact = physeq_filtered@sam_data${{ feature }},
  nperm = 9999
)

# Convertir a data frame para una tabla más clara
pairwise_df <- as.data.frame(pairwise_{{ feature }}$p.value)
colnames(pairwise_df) <- paste0("p-value (", colnames(pairwise_df), ")")

pairwise_df %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(., 5))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Pairwise comparisons PERMANOVA (p-values)")
```
